correctness.rationale: Cooper's level-13 modular formula supplies Z(X)^2=F(X) in Z[[X]], F(0)=1 and linear coefficient a=3. Expanding sqrt(1+I), 4^n binom(1/2,k) for the k-th term has v2=2(n-k)+s2(k); the inequality s2(n)<=s2(k)+(n-k) puts all k<n contributions above the k=n valuation s2(n). The unique k=n term has odd a^n, proving v2(S_n)=s2(n) for every n>=1. Terms k<=n-2 vanish modulo 2^{s2(n)+2}; the k=n-1 factor (n-1)a^{n-2}b has sufficient 2-adic valuation, yielding the exact Catalan congruence. Division by 4^n gives denominator 2^{2n-s2(n)}; binomial distribution of popcounts yields frequency C(m,k). Checked exact integer recurrence and congruence independently through n=121 plus source checker structure. The all-n theorem depends on Cooper's true modular square identity, not finite evidence.
residual_risks: Cooper's integral square is an essential previously published hypothesis; finite checker through 121 not an independent proof.
